title: Impact assessment
description: One schema for three assessments, told apart by `type`: an AI system impact assessment (aiia), an AI addendum to a data protection impact assessment (dpia_addendum) and a fundamental rights impact assessment (fria). Shared fields carry the risks, mitigations and outcome; type-specific fields carry what each instrument asks for.
$comment: AI Governance Engineer templates and schemas library, v1. CC BY 4.0 (attribution: Jorge García Aibar). x-evidences names the obligations a field or record helps evidence: an illustrative mapping, not a claim of conformity and not legal advice. https://aigovernanceengineer.com/resources/templates

$schema.description: The URI of this schema, so a record says what it claims to be.

type.description: Which assessment this is. aiia: AI system impact assessment (ISO/IEC 42005 style); dpia_addendum: AI-specific addendum to a GDPR DPIA; fria: fundamental rights impact assessment by a deployer.

subject.description: The governed object as registry id and version, "id@version" (for example "csa-01@2026-09-18"). The key every record is filed against.

consulted.description: Stakeholders and experts consulted, including representatives of affected groups.

related_assessments.description: Ids of related assessments. A FRIA may build on an existing DPIA rather than repeat it.

processes.description: fria: the deployer's processes in which the system is used, in line with its intended purpose.

period_and_frequency.description: fria: how long and how often the system will be used.

affected_categories.description: Categories of persons and groups likely to be affected.

processing_description.description: dpia_addendum: systematic description of the processing and its purposes, including the AI-specific steps (training, inference, retention of prompts and outputs).

necessity_and_proportionality.description: dpia_addendum: why the processing, and the use of AI for it, is necessary and proportionate.

ai_specific.description: dpia_addendum and aiia: questions a classic DPIA template does not ask.

training_vs_operational_data.description: How training data and operational data differ in source, basis and retention.

automated_decision_making.description: Whether decisions with legal or similarly significant effect are taken solely by automated means.

inferences.description: What the system infers about people, and whether those inferences are stored.

memorisation_and_extraction.description: Risk that personal data is memorised by the model and extracted from it.

risks.description: Specific risks of harm to the people and groups affected.

right_or_interest.description: The right, freedom or interest at stake (for example "non-discrimination", "privacy").

risk_register_id.description: Matching risk register entry, if any.

human_oversight_measures.description: fria: how the oversight measures in the instructions for use are implemented.

mitigations.description: Measures to take if the risks materialise, and measures to prevent them.

governance_and_complaints.description: fria: internal governance and complaint mechanisms if the risks materialise.

dpo_advice.description: dpia_addendum: the data protection officer's advice and how it was taken into account.

residual_risk.description: What remains after mitigation, in a sentence.

outcome.description: Outcome. prior_consultation_required applies when a DPIA shows high residual risk.

required.description: Whether the results must be notified to the market surveillance authority.

role.description: The approving role, not a personal name.

conditions.description: Conditions attached to the approval, if any.

signature.description: Detached signature over the record, prefixed with the algorithm (for example "ed25519:<base64>"). Makes the record tamper-evident in the evidence store.

review_triggers.description: Changes that reopen the assessment (new purpose, new data, new group affected, incident).

extensions.description: Organisation-specific fields. Validators ignore their content; keep evidence-bearing fields in the core record.
